clue.text: Incompetent bunch? I'm not sure after demonstration

indicators.note: after places the hesitation sound behind the word for a display

parts.note: a show is a demonstration or display
er is the hesitant noise of someone unsure

explanation.surface: Someone, unsure, judges a group of protesters to be useless after watching their march.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demonstration' suggests a protest march but simply means a display.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a shower is a hopeless, useless group of people, as in 'what a shower!'

clue.text: Sultry individual without an ID

indicators.note: without tells us to remove the word an from the word for a person

parts.note: a human is an individual person

explanation.surface: A sultry person turns up without any identification papers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'individual' is the noun, a person, not the adjective 'single'; 'without' is the deletion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sultry weather is hot and damp, which is exactly what humid describes.

clue.text: Friendly German keeps working for aggressive type

indicators.note: keeps means the friendly German holds the working word inside him

parts.note: a warm manner is a friendly one
a machine that is on is working

explanation.surface: An affable German keeps busy on behalf of a belligerent person.
explanation.definitionFit: A warmonger is someone who stirs up or pushes for war, an aggressive sort.

clue.text: Country game getting a lot of criticism

parts.note: RU stands for rugby union, a game

indicators.note: a lot of, but not all, so the criticism word loses its final letter

parts.note: stick is informal British for harsh criticism, as in 'taking stick'

explanation.surface: A country sport attracts plenty of disapproval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' trims STICK to STIC. RU is rugby union, the British football code played with an oval ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Country used as an adjective, as in country cottage, means rural, which is what rustic says.

clue.text: Breaking rib in a hurry to improve image

indicators.note: in places the jumbled rib inside a and hurry

parts.note: a rush is a hurry

indicators.note: breaking suggests the rib is shattered, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone cracks a rib while rushing to tidy up a photograph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' is the anagram signal, not a description of an injury; 'in' sets the result between the two other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To airbrush a photo is to retouch it so the subject looks better, improving the picture.

clue.text: Flounder — when caught out of place?

definitions.text: Flounder — when caught out of place?

parts.words: Flounder — when caught out of place?
parts.note: a flounder is a flatfish; once landed it is literally stranded in the wrong element, and the phrase means a person awkwardly out of place

explanation.surface: A puzzled person struggles when found somewhere they should not be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flounder' reads as the verb to struggle, but is also the flatfish, which once caught is literally beached.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone uncomfortable in unfamiliar surroundings, just like a landed fish gasping on the bank.

clue.text: Restraint needed during calls for locks

indicators.note: during puts the restraint inside the word for calls, as it falls within them

parts.note: rings means telephone calls
let is an old word for hindrance, kept in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: Holding back is required while phoning a locksmith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locks' suggests doors, but means hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Ringlets are curly locks of hair, so they are a kind of locks.

clue.text: Runs and manages to find missing leader

indicators.note: missing leader means the word for finding loses its opening letter

parts.note: traces means tracks down or manages to find

explanation.surface: Someone sprints and succeeds in finding someone who has gone missing.
explanation.definitionFit: Runs as a noun, sprints or contests on foot, are races.

clue.text: Master criminal picking everything up must be suspect

indicators.note: picking, as in picking up, means the scrambled master gathers the reversed word inside it
criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so master is rearranged
up in a down clue tells us the word for everything is read from bottom to top

parts.note: all means everything

explanation.surface: A crime boss scooping everything up ought to be under suspicion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Master criminal' reads as one phrase, a mastermind, but 'criminal' is the anagram signal on 'Master' alone; 'up' works because this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom meaning to suspect that something is wrong.

clue.text: Belief in keeping new promises

indicators.note: keeping means the word in holds the reshaped letters between its own two
new suggests a fresh version, so the letters of promises are reshaped

explanation.surface: Someone has faith in keeping freshly made pledges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a link word here but a piece that does the keeping, its two letters splitting to hold the rearranged pledges.
explanation.definitionFit: An impression is a vague notion or belief, as in 'I was under the impression'.

clue.text: Signals last of sugar to be removed from preserves

indicators.note: to be removed from means that letter is taken out of the word for preserves

parts.note: cures means preserves, as with smoking or salting meat

indicators.note: last of picks the final letter of sugar

explanation.surface: Signals that sugar should be left out of jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'preserves' looks like the noun jam, but is the verb cures; R is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Cues are prompts or signs telling someone when to act, as in theatre.

clue.text: Tick off day being hugged by a beautiful person

indicators.note: being hugged by means the day sits inside a and the attractive person

parts.note: a dish is informal for an attractive person
MON is the short form of Monday

explanation.surface: Someone is reprimanded on the day a gorgeous partner gives them a cuddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tick off' means reprimand, not mark with a tick.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick off is British slang for reprimanding, which is what admonish means.

clue.text: In conclusion, the French play regularly on street

indicators.note: on means the picked letters come after the street abbreviation

parts.note: la is a French word for the

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of play, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: A French drama is finally staged on a regular basis in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes LY from pLaY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lastly is a word used to introduce a final point, as in conclusion does.

clue.text: Report of name being held in reserve

indicators.note: being held in places the name letter within the reserving word

parts.note: to bag something, such as a seat, is to reserve it

explanation.surface: An account of a famous name kept as backup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' is a loud noise here, not a written account.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp sound of a gun firing, a bang.

clue.text: Promise confidence

explanation.surface: Two near-synonyms, a pledge and self-belief, set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Assurance covers both a firm promise and a poised self-confidence.

clue.text: Unit dismissing one old part of hospital is inconvenient

indicators.note: dismissing means unit sends away the numeral one

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a ward is a room or section of a hospital

explanation.surface: A department sacking a former member of a hospital ward is awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dismissing' turns UNIT into UNT.
explanation.definitionFit: Untoward means unexpected and unwelcome, causing trouble, close to inconvenient.

clue.text: Fish and wine perhaps a bit off

parts.note: white is a type of wine, signalled by perhaps

indicators.note: off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters of a bit are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seafood supper where the wine tastes slightly spoiled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' turns A BIT into BAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitebait are the small young fry of herring and sprats, eaten whole as a fish dish.

clue.text: Sorry impasse surrounding Conservative flight from reality

indicators.note: surrounding means the scrambled impasse wraps round the party letter
sorry means in a poor state, so impasse is rearranged

explanation.surface: A wretched political deadlock around a Tory leads someone to retreat from the real world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' turns IMPASSE into ESAPISM, which wraps C.
explanation.definitionFit: Escapism is seeking distraction from unpleasant real life through fantasy or entertainment.

clue.text: Drink may be essential to best journalists only at first

indicators.note: the essential part of a word is its heart, so the central letters of best

parts.note: the press means journalists collectively

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of only

explanation.surface: Coffee might be vital to top reporters, at least at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential to best' gives ES, the core of bESt.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee, a drink.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about, if not moving without force

indicators.note: moving means the letters of if not are stirred about and rearranged
without means the force letter is left out of the mix

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for force in physics

explanation.surface: Keen on it, unless the thing stays still without any push.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges IF NOT; 'without' drops F, leaving the four letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To be into something is informal for being keen on or enthusiastic about it.

clue.text: Unusually gifted, one's always on the move

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters of gifted are arranged in an unusual way

explanation.surface: An exceptionally talented person never sits still.
explanation.definitionFit: A fidget is a restless person who keeps shifting about and can never keep still.

clue.text: Dar es Salaam sadly lacking sales fleet

indicators.note: sadly means the city name is in a bad way, so its letters are rearranged
lacking means the letters of sales are missing from the mix

explanation.surface: The Tanzanian port's trade slumps, leaving its ships idle.
explanation.walkthrough: Dar es Salaam, the Tanzanian port, has eleven letters; 'lacking' drops S, A, L, E, S and 'sadly' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a large fleet of warships, after the Spanish Armada.

clue.text: Trouble from elements in stag groups?

indicators.note: elements in says the answer is made up of letters found within stag groups

explanation.surface: Bother comes from bunches of rowdy stag parties.
explanation.walkthrough: A stag party is a British pre-wedding night out for the groom and his friends; the answer sits in stAG GROups.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggro is British slang for aggressive trouble or hassle.

clue.text: Send a letter of request as result of vehicle collision

definitions.meaning: to send away a letter asking for it
a car so damaged it is not worth repairing

explanation.surface: A letter asking for compensation after a car crash.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb phrase means to apply by post; the noun is a vehicle declared beyond repair after a crash.

clue.text: Extra meat after changing sides

indicators.note: changing sides means left becomes right, so L in the meat word is swapped for R

parts.note: flesh is meat

explanation.surface: Additional meat is served after a team switches ends.
explanation.walkthrough: L and R stand for left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh can mean additional or further, as in fresh supplies, an extra lot.

clue.text: Well-provided-for, having arms from the east

indicators.note: from the east in an across clue means read right to left, so the weapons word runs backwards

parts.note: guns are arms or weapons

explanation.surface: A comfortably-off person has been armed by an eastern supplier.
explanation.definitionFit: Snug can mean comfortable and secure, well off enough to be content.

clue.text: Some decide target night should be rejected as unified

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the extracted run of letters is read backwards
some means only part of the words decide target night is used

explanation.surface: Choosing a goal for the evening is thrown out as being joined up.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters deCIDE TARGET NIght, read right to left, give IN TEGRAT ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Integrated means combined into a whole, unified.

clue.text: Case of remarkable one-time revolutionary

indicators.note: case of gives the outside letters of remarkable, like its casing

parts.note: former means one-time or previous

explanation.surface: An instance of an extraordinary ex-rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of remarkable' gives RE, its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A reformer seeks radical change, which a loose sense of revolutionary covers.

clue.text: Easily irritated, I will leave the City in turmoil

indicators.note: will leave means the letter I departs from the mix
in turmoil means the letters of the city are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A cranky banker quits London's financial district amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is London's financial district. 'will leave' drops I from THECITY and 'in turmoil' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetchy means bad-tempered and irritable, quick to take offence.
